edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource, from the Wen Xuan anthology
edition.zh: 据维基文库所录《昭明文选》本

basis.en: Written in the early third century; the author died in 226.
basis.zh: 作于三世纪初，作者卒于 226 年。

note.en: Cao Pi wrote this as crown prince of Wei, and it is usually counted the first Chinese essay devoted to literature as such: how writers misjudge one another, why each form asks for different virtues, and why a style cannot be handed on. It ends with the claim that writing is ‘a splendid undertaking that does not decay’, outlasting both a lifetime and its honours. Notice that he ranks the Seven Masters of Jian’an even as he misses them; several had died in the epidemic of 217.
note.zh: 曹丕作为魏国太子时写下这篇文章，它通常被视为中国第一篇专门讨论文学本身的论文：文人怎样彼此误判，不同的文体为什么要求不同的长处，文风为什么无法传授。它以这样的论断收尾：文章是“不朽之盛事”，比寿命和荣华都更长久。留意他一边品评建安七子，一边怀念他们；其中好几位死于 217 年的那场疫病。

excerpt.orig: 蓋文章經國之大業，不朽之盛事。
excerpt.en: For writing is the great work of ordering a state, a splendid undertaking that does not decay.
excerpt.zh: 盖文章经国之大业，不朽之盛事。

gloss.en: The opening phrase became a proverb for the way writers look down on one another.
gloss.zh: 这句开篇语后来成为成语，指文人之间互相轻视。

gloss.en: Fu Yi (d. c. 90), styled Wuzhong, a writer of the Eastern Han who served alongside Ban Gu as an archivist of the Orchid Terrace.
gloss.zh: 傅毅（？—约 90），字武仲，东汉文学家，曾与班固同在兰台校书。

gloss.en: Ban Gu (32–92), historian and rhapsodist of the Eastern Han, author of the History of the Former Han.
gloss.zh: 班固（32—92），东汉史学家、辞赋家，著《汉书》。

gloss.en: Between the eldest and the second brother: so close that there is little to choose between them.
gloss.zh: 伯、仲是兄弟排行中的老大、老二。比喻不相上下。

gloss.en: Ban Chao (32–102), Ban Gu’s younger brother, the general who restored Han power in the Western Regions.
gloss.zh: 班超（32—102），班固之弟，东汉名将，长期经营西域。

gloss.en: An officer of the Orchid Terrace, the Han palace library and archive, in charge of documents and the collation of books.
gloss.zh: 兰台是汉代宫中藏书和档案之所；兰台令史掌管文书、校订典籍。

gloss.en: The source of the idiom 敝帚自珍, to treasure one’s own worn-out broom.
gloss.zh: 后来凝成成语“敝帚自珍”。

gloss.en: This passage is the origin of the name ‘Seven Masters of the Jian’an era’ (建安七子) for the writers gathered around the Cao family.
gloss.zh: “建安七子”这一名称即源于此。

gloss.en: Two names for thoroughbred horses; 騄 recalls Lu’er (騄耳), one of the eight steeds of King Mu of Zhou.
gloss.zh: 都是良马。騄，即騄耳，相传为周穆王八骏之一。

gloss.en: The manner of Qi. Xu Gan came from Beihai, in the old land of Qi, whose writing was thought slow and leisurely.
gloss.zh: 齐地的习气。徐幹是北海人，属古齐地；当时人认为齐地文风舒缓。

gloss.en: Wang Can’s ‘Rhapsody on Climbing the Tower’, written while he was a refugee in Jingzhou, the best known of the works named here.
gloss.zh: 王粲的《登楼赋》，作于避乱荆州之时，是这里所举作品中最有名的一篇。

gloss.en: Zhang Heng (78–139) and Cai Yong (133–192), the great rhapsodists of the Eastern Han.
gloss.zh: 张衡（78—139）和蔡邕（133—192），东汉著名的辞赋家。

gloss.en: Four kinds of official prose: 章 and 表, memorials to the throne; 書, letters; 記, notes and dispatches. Chen Lin and Ruan Yu drafted such documents for Cao Cao.
gloss.zh: 四种文体：章、表是呈给皇帝的奏章，书是书信，记是公文笺记。陈琳、阮瑀曾为曹操掌管这类文书。

gloss.en: Kong Rong (153–208), a descendant of Confucius famous for his wit; Cao Cao had him put to death in 208.
gloss.zh: 孔融（153—208），孔子后裔，以才辩著称，208 年被曹操所杀。

gloss.en: Yang Xiong (53 BCE–18 CE) and Ban Gu, masters of Han rhapsody and prose.
gloss.zh: 扬雄（前 53—18）和班固，汉代辞赋与文章的大家。

gloss.en: Inscriptions cut on vessels or stones, and dirges that recount the life of the dead: both should keep to the facts.
gloss.zh: 铭，刻在器物或碑石上的文字；诔，哀悼死者、叙述其生平的文章。二者都应当崇尚真实。

gloss.en: 氣 (qi): the vital breath or temperament a writer is born with. This sentence began the long tradition of judging writing by its qi.
gloss.zh: 气：作者天赋的气质与才性。这一说法开了后世以“气”论文的传统。

gloss.en: 檢: a rule or measure. The rhythm keeps to the same measure.
gloss.zh: 检：法度。节奏遵循同样的法度。

gloss.en: 經國: to govern and set the state in order.
gloss.zh: 经国：治理国家。

gloss.en: The Lord of the West, later honoured as King Wen of Zhou, was imprisoned at Youli by the last Shang king; tradition says he worked out the sixty-four hexagrams of the Changes there.
gloss.zh: 西伯即周文王。相传他被商纣王囚禁在羑里时，推演出《周易》的六十四卦。

gloss.en: Ji Dan, the Duke of Zhou, regent for the young King Cheng, is credited with setting down the rites of Zhou.
gloss.zh: 周公姬旦，辅佐年幼的成王摄政，相传制礼作乐。

gloss.en: In hardship and obscurity.
gloss.zh: 处境困厄，不得志。

gloss.en: After a saying in the Huainanzi: the sage does not prize a jade disc a foot across, but values an inch of the sundial’s shadow, for time is hard to gain and easy to lose.
gloss.zh: 语出《淮南子·原道训》：“圣人不贵尺之璧，而重寸之阴，时难得而易失也。”

gloss.en: To change along with all things: a way of saying to die.
gloss.zh: 随万物一同变化，指死亡。

gloss.en: Xu Gan’s treatise is the Zhong lun (Balanced Discourses), which survives.
gloss.zh: 徐幹著有《中论》，今存。

gloss.en: A school or teaching of one’s own, the phrase Sima Qian used of his own history.
gloss.zh: 自成体系的学说。语本司马迁《报任安书》“成一家之言”。

note.en: Usually counted the first Chinese essay on literature as such, sharp on why writers belittle one another; uneven, but its claim for writing as lasting work set a tradition.
note.zh: 通常被视为中国第一篇专论文学的文章，“文人相轻”说得透彻；行文不甚匀称，但“文章不朽”之论开启了传统。
